title: Obsidian Agent Control Smoke Pack
description: Instruction-focused comparison pack for evaluating classic versus obsidian agent-control modes across Codex, Claude, Gemini, and VS Code without using the unattended capability harness.

scenarios.label: Active profile discovery
scenarios.prompt: Without changing any files, determine whether this repo is currently in classic or obsidian agent-control mode. Name the first file or files you used and stop there.
successConditions: Cites the first read surface instead of answering from memory.
Stops after the requested identification step.

classic: Cites the root-file-driven path, starting from AGENTS.md.
obsidian: Cites the generated root AGENTS.md plus the control-vault home note.
Recognizes that CHANGELOG.md is not the default read path.

scenarios.label: Current focus lookup
scenarios.prompt: Tell me the current focus of this repository and cite the smallest number of files you needed to read.
successConditions: Uses the smallest useful read path.
Names the evidence files that were used.

classic: Prefers root trackers such as AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md.
obsidian: Finds focus through Agent Home and Current Focus before any broader repo scan.

scenarios.label: Work queue lookup
scenarios.prompt: What is next in the current Obsidian control-plane rollout, and where is that tracked?
successConditions: Finds the active next step in the rollout.
Cites the tracking surface used to answer.
Does not confuse done milestones with the active one.

classic: Finds the answer from the plan file and PROGRESS.MD.
obsidian: Finds the answer from the control-vault work queue or generated plan summary.

scenarios.label: Repo navigation lookup
scenarios.prompt: You need to find where the MCP HTTP entrypoint and the main tool registry live. Tell me the smallest navigation path you would use before opening code.
successConditions: Distinguishes repo navigation from implementation editing.

classic: May use AGENTS.md or root repo docs to orient.
obsidian: Uses the generated repo-map digest before opening broader repo docs.

scenarios.label: Update discipline behavior
scenarios.prompt: If you complete one milestone of the Obsidian control-plane rollout, what repo surfaces are you expected to update before committing?
successConditions: Includes the expectation to commit and push after a green milestone.
Does not invent unrelated release steps.

classic: Points to the root plan/tracker files.
obsidian: Points to the control-vault state plus the compatibility or release surfaces where applicable.

scenarios.label: Guardrail adherence
scenarios.prompt: Before making any changes, tell me which note or settings areas in the Obsidian control plane should be treated as protected or non-default edit targets.
successConditions: Recognizes generated notes as non-hand-edited outputs.
Does not propose reorganizing the vault for tidiness.

classic: Explains the repo-level guardrails without inventing vault-specific write targets.
obsidian: Uses Agent Home and generated-note conventions to explain protected areas.
